views.observation: Narrow local peg pass: the selected central needle has a short angular connector projecting from the polygonal twig edge before widening into its shaft. Contact is directly visible here; this does not establish either complete socket or the other angles.

The selected connector runs almost across the twig face. Its narrow straight proximal section is visible, but the actual base relief is superimposed on wood; this angle remains insufficient for an independent contact pass.

The selected narrow connector extends beyond the twig silhouette, but the near twig face hides its origin at the central attachment point. Relief is visible; complete polygonal base contact remains unassessed from this angle.
Needle-bearing polygonal twig is visible, but overlapping large needles obscure enough of the selected small connector to withhold an independent peg/contact pass.
The selected contact is superimposed with the twig and crossing needles; no unobscured complete peg base is resolved at this angle.
The selected origin lies behind the near twig face; surrounding radial needles are visible but cannot establish the hidden contact. Unassessed peg base at this angle.

A small proximal connector projects from the lower twig edge into the central downward needle. Local peg relief is discernible; this view does not establish the full alternate socket or transfer acceptance to the first target.
The near broad needle overlaps the selected contact region at the central twig edge; peg base acceptance is withheld, independently of the pass-4 alternate-left observation.
Polygonal needle shafts and narrow proximal transitions are visible, but the selected central origin is on the far side of the near twig face. This angle does not establish its hidden base contact.

The pinned departing axis is the lower-left arm. Its near-side polygonal surface reaches the supporting wood without a visible empty gap; this provides a narrow local continuity observation. Needles and the supporting face still hide part of the junction circumference, so complete socket anatomy is not accepted.

The departing woody arm meets the support, but its rounded butt/collar edge and an overlying needle obscure the full socket transition. No disconnected gap is diagnosed; complete socket fidelity remains unassessed.
The near supporting surface and crossing needles hide the selected branch emergence. Visible neighbouring wood is insufficient evidence for the hidden socket.

The near face of the selected twig-parent junction is visibly connected with a narrowing departing axis and no empty gap. A needle overlaps its upper transition, limiting this to a local continuity observation rather than complete all-angle acceptance.
The joint is aligned behind the near woody axis and a broad needle. The connected whole scene is preserved, but this angle cannot establish the obscured twig-parent socket.

The departing twig reaches its supporting axis visibly along the lower near edge, but the central upper transition is covered by a broad needle. This supplements local continuity without establishing the full socket.
